translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Liu Zunkao was moved from Right to Left Vice Director, and Wang Silang, prefect of Danyang, was appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁卯，詔上林苑內士庶丘墓欲還合葬者，勿禁。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on dingmao, an edict declared that commoners whose ancestral tombs lay within Shanglin Park who wished to reinter their dead in joint burial should not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on dingmao, an edict declared that families whose ancestral graves lay in Shanglin Park and wished to reinter their dead together should not be prevented.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月癸未，詔克日於玄武湖大閱水師，並巡江右，講武校獵。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the seventh year, on guiwei, an edict fixed a day for a grand review of the navy on Xuanwu Lake, together with a tour of the lands west of the river, military drills, and a hunting review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the seventh year, on guiwei, an edict fixed a date for a grand naval review on Xuanwu Lake, a tour of the lands west of the Yangtze, military exercises, and a hunting expedition.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以右衛將軍顏師伯為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On dinghai, General of the Right Guard Yan Shibo was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai General of the Right Guard Yan Shibo was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 二月甲寅，車駕巡南豫、南兗二州。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiayin, the imperial carriage toured the two provinces of Southern Yu and Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiayin, the emperor toured Southern Yu and Southern Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，校獵烏江。

translations.literal: On dingsi, a hunting review was held at Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi a hunting expedition was held at Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 己未，登烏江縣六合山。

translations.literal: On jiwei, he ascended Liuhe Mountain in Wujiang County.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he climbed Liuhe Mountain in Wujiang County.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，大赦，行幸所經，無出今年租布，賜人爵一級，女子百戶牛酒，郡守邑宰及人夫從搜者，普加沾賚。

translations.literal: On renxu, a general amnesty; along the route of the imperial progress, land tax and cloth levies for the current year were remitted; each person was granted one rank of nobility; a hundred households of women were given cattle and wine; prefects, magistrates, and laborers who joined the hunt all received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu a general amnesty was proclaimed; along the route of the imperial tour, land tax and cloth levies for the current year were remitted, each person was granted one rank of nobility, a hundred households of women received cattle and wine, and prefects, magistrates, and laborers who joined the hunt were all rewarded.

sentences.zh: 又詔蠲曆陽郡租輸三年，遣使巡慰，問人疾苦。

translations.literal: An edict also remitted three years of tax and tribute for Liyang Commandery and dispatched envoys to tour and comfort the people, inquiring after their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also remitted three years of tax and tribute for Liyang Commandery and dispatched envoys to tour the region, comfort the people, and inquire after their hardships.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，行幸尉氏，觀溫泉。

translations.literal: On guihai, the emperor traveled to Weishi to view the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the emperor traveled to Weishi to view the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 壬申，車駕至都，拜二廟，乃還宮。

translations.literal: On renshen, the imperial carriage reached the capital, paid homage at the two ancestral temples, and then returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the imperial procession reached the capital, paid homage at the two ancestral temples, and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子，詔自今非臨軍戰陣，一不得專殺；

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on jiazi, an edict declared: from now on, except on the battlefield in active combat, no one may kill on his own authority;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiazi, an edict declared: henceforth, except in the heat of battle, no one may execute another on his own authority;

sentences.zh: 其罪入重辟者，皆依舊先上須報，有司嚴加聽察，犯者以殺人罪論。

translations.literal: those whose crimes warrant capital punishment must, as before, first report upward and await approval; officials were strictly enjoined to investigate, and violators were to be judged for the crime of murder.
translations.idiomatic: those whose crimes warrant capital punishment must, as before, report upward and await approval; officials were strictly ordered to investigate, and violators were to be punished as murderers.

sentences.zh: 五月丙子，詔自今刺史守宰動人興軍，皆須手詔施行；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingzi, an edict declared: from now on, when provincial inspectors and prefectural magistrates mobilize men and raise armies, they must all act on a personally written imperial edict;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingzi, an edict declared: henceforth, when provincial inspectors and prefectural magistrates mobilize troops, they must do so only on the basis of a personally written imperial edict;

sentences.zh: 惟邊隅外警及奸釁內發，變起倉卒者，不從此例。

translations.literal: only when there is alarm on the borderlands or sedition breaks out within, and crisis arises suddenly, was this rule not to apply.
translations.idiomatic: only when alarm came from the frontiers or sedition erupted within and crisis arose suddenly was this rule not to apply.

sentences.zh: 六月戊申，蠕蠕、高麗等國並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wushen, Rouran, Goguryeo, and other states all sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, Rouran, Goguryeo, and other states all sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙亥，進高麗王高璉位車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on yihai, King Gao Lian of Goguryeo was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on yihai, King Gao Lian of Goguryeo was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 八月乙丑，立皇子子孟為淮南王、子產為臨賀王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yichou, the imperial son Zimeng was established as Prince of Huainan and Zichan as Prince of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou, the imperial son Zimeng was enfeoffed as Prince of Huainan and Zichan as Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸建康、秣陵縣訊獄囚。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited Jiankang and Moling County to hear criminal cases and examine prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Jiankang and Moling County to hear criminal cases and examine prisoners.

sentences.zh: 九月庚寅，以南徐州刺史新安王子鸞為兼司徒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was made Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was made Acting Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 乙未，幸廷尉訊獄囚。

translations.literal: On yiwei, he visited the Court of Justice to hear criminal cases and examine prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he visited the Court of Justice to hear criminal cases and examine prisoners.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立皇子子嗣為東平王。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the imperial son Zisi was established as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the imperial son Zisi was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，皇太子冠，賜王公以下帛各有差。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on renyin, the crown prince received his capping; princes and officials down to the lowest ranks were given silk according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renyin, the crown prince received his capping ceremony; princes and officials of every rank were granted silk according to their station.

sentences.zh: 戊申，車駕巡南豫州，奉太后以行。

translations.literal: On wushen, the imperial carriage toured Southern Yu Province, bringing the empress dowager along.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the emperor toured Southern Yu Province, bringing the empress dowager with him.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，行幸江寧縣訊獄囚。

translations.literal: On guichou, the emperor traveled to Jiangning County to hear criminal cases and examine prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he traveled to Jiangning County to hear criminal cases and examine prisoners.

sentences.zh: 加車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, was granted privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, General of Chariots and Cavalry and inspector of Yangzhou, was granted privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以開府儀同三司東海王褘為司空，加中軍將軍義陽王昶開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On guihai, Prince Hui of Donghai, with privilege equal to the Three Dukes, was made Minister of Works; and General of the Center, Prince Chang of Yiyang, was granted privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Prince Hui of Donghai, already holding privilege equal to the Three Dukes, was made Minister of Works, and Prince Chang of Yiyang, General of the Center, was granted the same privilege.

sentences.zh: 己巳，校獵于姑孰。

translations.literal: On jisi, a hunting review was held at Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi a hunting expedition was held at Gudu.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙子，曲赦南豫州殊死以下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingzi, a partial amnesty was granted for crimes below capital punishment in Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingzi, a partial amnesty was granted in Southern Yu Province for all crimes short of capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 巡幸所經，詳減今歲田租。

translations.literal: Along the route of the imperial tour, land tax for the current year was substantially reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route of the imperial tour, land tax for the current year was substantially reduced.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔祭晉大司馬桓溫、征西將軍毛璩墓。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict ordered sacrifices at the tombs of Huan Wen, Grand Marshal of Jin, and Mao Yu, General Pacifying the West.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou an edict ordered sacrifices at the tombs of Huan Wen, Grand Marshal of Jin, and Mao Yu, General Pacifying the West.

sentences.zh: 上于行所訊溧陽、永世、丹陽縣囚。

translations.literal: The emperor heard cases and examined prisoners in Liyang, Yongshi, and Danyang counties at his stopping places.
translations.idiomatic: At his stopping places the emperor heard cases and examined prisoners in Liyang, Yongshi, and Danyang counties.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，祀梁山，大閱水師。

translations.literal: On guisi, sacrifices were performed at Liangshan, and the navy was grandly reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi sacrifices were performed at Liangshan and the navy was reviewed in full array.

sentences.zh: 于中江，有白雀二集華蓋，有司奏改元為神雀，詔不許。

translations.literal: On the middle reaches of the river, two white sparrows alighted on the imperial parasol; officials memorialized to change the era name to Shenque, but the edict did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: On the middle reaches of the river two white sparrows alighted on the imperial parasol; officials memorialized to change the era name to Shenque, but the emperor did not approve.

sentences.zh: 乙未，原放行獄徒系。

translations.literal: On yiwei, convicts and bondsmen in prison were pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei convicts and bondsmen in prison were pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 浙江東諸郡大旱。

translations.literal: The commanderies east of the Zhe River suffered severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies east of the Zhe River suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬寅，遣使開倉賑恤，聽受雜物當租。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renyin, envoys were dispatched to open granaries for relief; miscellaneous goods were accepted in lieu of land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renyin, envoys were dispatched to open granaries for relief, and miscellaneous goods were accepted in lieu of land tax.

sentences.zh: 丙午，行幸曆陽。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the emperor traveled to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor traveled to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦，賜曆陽郡女子百戶牛酒，蠲郡租十年。

translations.literal: On jiayin, a general amnesty; a hundred households of women in Liyang Commandery were given cattle and wine, and the commandery's land tax was remitted for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin a general amnesty was proclaimed; a hundred households of women in Liyang Commandery received cattle and wine, and the commandery's land tax was remitted for ten years.

sentences.zh: 己未，加太宰江夏王義恭尚書令。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was additionally made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was additionally made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 于博望梁山立雙闕。

translations.literal: At Liangshan in Bowang, paired gate towers were erected.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangshan in Bowang, paired gate towers were erected.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，至自曆陽。

translations.literal: On guihai, he returned from Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he returned from Liyang.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月辛巳，祀南郊。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the eighth year, on xisi, the southern suburbs were sacrificed to.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the eighth year, on xisi, the emperor sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 是日，還宗祀文帝於明堂。

translations.literal: That same day, Emperor Wen was again sacrificed to in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he performed the associated rite in the Bright Hall, honoring Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔曰：「東境去歲不稔，宜廣商貨，遠近販鬻米粟者，可停道中雜稅。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict declared: "Last year the eastern regions had a poor harvest; trade in grain should be encouraged. Those who buy and sell rice and millet near and far may be exempted from miscellaneous taxes on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu an edict declared: "Last year the eastern regions had a poor harvest; grain trade should be encouraged. Those who buy and sell rice and millet near and far shall be exempt from miscellaneous taxes on the roads.

sentences.zh: 其以仗自防，悉勿禁。」

translations.literal: Those who carry weapons for self-defense—none of this is to be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: Those who carry weapons for self-defense—none of this shall be forbidden."

sentences.zh: 夏閏五月壬寅，乙太宰江夏王義恭領太尉。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of summer, on renyin, Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of summer, on renyin, Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝崩於玉燭殿，時年三十五。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the emperor died in the Hall of the Jade Candle at the age of thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the emperor died in the Hall of the Jade Candle at the age of thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 七月丙午，葬於丹陽秣陵縣岩山景寧陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on bingwu, he was buried at Jingning Mausoleum on Yanshan in Moling County, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on bingwu, he was buried at Jingning Mausoleum on Yanshan in Moling County, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝末年為長夜之飲，每旦寢興，盥嗽畢，仍復命飲，俄頃數斗，憑幾惛睡，若大醉者。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor held feasts that lasted through the night; each morning when he rose, after washing and rinsing he would again order wine, and in an instant would consume several pecks; leaning on his armrest he would fall into a stupor like a man deeply drunk.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor held feasts that lasted through the night; each morning after rising and washing he would again order wine and in an instant consume several pecks; leaning on his armrest he would sink into a stupor like a man deeply drunk.

sentences.zh: 或外有奏事，便肅然整容，無復酒色。

translations.literal: Yet when business came from outside, he would at once compose his bearing with solemn dignity, with no trace of drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when business arrived from outside, he would at once compose his bearing with solemn dignity, with no trace of drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 外內服其神明，莫敢弛惰。

translations.literal: Within and without, all submitted to his clarity of mind, and none dared slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without, all submitted to his clarity of mind, and none dared slacken.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝諱子業，小字法師，孝武帝長子也。

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Ziye, his childhood name Fashi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor's taboo name was Ziye, his childhood name Fashi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年正月甲申生。

translations.literal: He was born on jiashen in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on jiashen in the first month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮尋陽，帝留都下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu garrisoned Xunyang, the emperor remained in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu garrisoned Xunyang, the prince remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 三十年，孝武入伐，元凶囚帝于侍中下省，將加害者數矣，卒得無恙。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Xiaowu marched east in punitive campaign, the Crown Prince Usurper imprisoned the emperor in the subordinate quarters of the Palace Attendants' office and several times was on the point of harming him, yet in the end he came through unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Xiaowu marched east in punitive campaign, the Crown Prince Usurper imprisoned the prince in the subordinate quarters of the Palace Attendants' office and several times was on the point of killing him, yet in the end he came through unharmed.

sentences.zh: 及孝武踐阼，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 始未之東宮，中庶子、二率併入直永福省。

translations.literal: At first, before he went to the Eastern Palace, the Palace Preceptor and the two Guard Commanders all entered duty together at Yongfu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before he moved to the Eastern Palace, the Palace Preceptor and the two Guard Commanders all entered duty together at Yongfu Province.

sentences.zh: 大明二年，出居東宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daming, he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 七年，加元服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he received his capping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he received his capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 八年閏五月庚申，孝武崩，其日，太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year, Emperor Xiaowu died; that same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the intercalary fifth month of the eighth year Emperor Xiaowu died; that same day the crown prince assumed the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 加驃騎大將軍柳元景尚書令。

translations.literal: General of Fast Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was additionally made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: General of Fast Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was additionally made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 甲子，置錄尚書官，乙太宰江夏王義恭錄尚書事，加驃騎大將軍柳元景開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was made Recorder of the Masters of Writing; General of Fast Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was granted privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the office of Recorder of the Masters of Writing was established; Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was made Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and General of Fast Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was granted privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚戌，婆皇國遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on gengxu, Po Huang sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on gengxu, Po Huang sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 崇皇太后為太皇太后，皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager was elevated to Empress Grand Dowager; the empress was titled Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager was elevated to Empress Grand Dowager, and the empress was titled Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，罷南北二馳道，改孝建以來所變制度，還依元嘉。

translations.literal: On yimao, the northern and southern speedways were abolished, and the institutions altered since Xiaojian were restored to the Yuanjia model.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the northern and southern speedways were abolished, and the institutions altered since Xiaojian were restored to the Yuanjia model.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，追崇獻妃為獻皇后。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Consort Xian was posthumously honored as Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 八月己丑，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jichou, the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jichou, the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 九月乙卯，文穆皇后祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, Empress Wenmu was buried alongside him at Jingning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yimao, Empress Wenmu was buried alongside him at Jingning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月乙酉，以尚書左僕射顏師伯為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter, on yiyou, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, on yiyou, Left Vice Director Yan Shibo was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以王畿諸郡為揚州，以揚州為東揚州。

translations.literal: On renchen, the commanderies of the metropolitan region were made Yang Province, and Yang Province was renamed Eastern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the commanderies of the metropolitan region were made Yang Province, and Yang Province was renamed Eastern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，加車騎將軍、揚州刺史豫章王子尚位司徒。

translations.literal: On guisi, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, was promoted to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, General of Chariots and Cavalry and inspector of Yangzhou, was promoted to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 去歲及是歲，東諸郡大旱，甚者米一斗數百，都下亦至百餘，餓死者十六七。

translations.literal: The previous year and this year the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the hardest-hit places a peck of rice cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital it reached over a hundred; sixteen or seventeen tenths of those who starved died.
translations.idiomatic: The previous year and this year the eastern commanderies suffered severe drought; in the hardest-hit places a peck of rice cost several hundred cash, and even in the capital over a hundred; of those who starved, sixteen or seventeen in ten died.

sentences.zh: 孝建以來，又立錢署鑄錢，百姓因此盜鑄，錢轉偽小，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since Xiaojian, mint offices had also been established to cast coin; the people therefore counterfeited in secret, and the money grew false and light until commerce ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaojian mint offices had also been established to cast coin; the people therefore counterfeited in secret, and the money grew false and light until commerce ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 景和元年春正月乙未朔，大赦，改元為永光。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the first day of the first month of spring in the first year of Yuanhe, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the first day of the first month of spring in the first year of Yuanhe, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，省諸州台傳。

translations.literal: On yisi, the relay stations of the provinces were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the provincial relay stations were abolished.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑，減州郡縣田祿之半。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yichou, the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, the field stipends of provinces, commanderies, and counties were reduced by half.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，鑄二銖錢。

translations.literal: On gengyin, two-zhu coins were cast.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin two-zhu coins were cast.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，魏文成皇帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Emperor Wencheng of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer Emperor Wencheng of Wei died.

sentences.zh: 秋八月庚午，以尚書僕射顏師伯為左僕射，吏部尚書王景文為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on gengwu, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shibo was made Left Vice Director, and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn, on gengwu, Vice Director Yan Shibo was made Left Vice Director, and Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Jingwen was made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自率宿衛兵誅太宰江夏王義恭、尚書令柳元景、左僕射顏師伯、廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the emperor himself led the palace guard to execute Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director Yan Shibo, and Director of Justice Liu Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor himself led the palace guard to execute Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yuanjing, Left Vice Director Yan Shibo, and Director of Justice Liu Deyuan.

sentences.zh: 改元為景和。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以司徒、揚州刺史豫章王子尚領尚書令。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Minister of Education and Inspector of Yangzhou, Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Prince Zishang of Yuzhang, Minister of Education and inspector of Yangzhou, was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝釋素服，禦錦衣。

translations.literal: On yihai, the emperor put off mourning dress and assumed brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the emperor put off mourning dress and assumed brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 以始興公沈慶之為太尉。

translations.literal: Duke Shen Qingzhi of Shixing was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shen Qingzhi of Shixing was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以石頭城為長樂宮，東府城為未央宮。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Shitou City was made Everlasting Joy Palace, and the Eastern Palace City was made Weiyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Shitou City was renamed Everlasting Joy Palace and the Eastern Palace City was renamed Weiyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以北邸為建章宮，南第為長楊宮。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Northern Residence was made Jianzhang Palace, and the Southern Manor was made Evergreen Poplar Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the Northern Residence was renamed Jianzhang Palace and the Southern Manor was renamed Evergreen Poplar Palace.

sentences.zh: 己丑，復立南北二馳道。

translations.literal: On jichou, the northern and southern speedways were reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the northern and southern speedways were reestablished.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，甯朔將軍何邁下獄死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renchen, General Pacifying the North He Mai died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renchen, General Pacifying the North He Mai died in prison.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，殺新除太尉沈慶之。

translations.literal: On guisi, the newly appointed Grand Commandant Shen Qingzhi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the newly appointed Grand Commandant Shen Qingzhi was killed.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，四廂奏樂。

translations.literal: On renyin, Lady Lu was established as empress, with music performed in four wings.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Lady Lu was established as empress, with music performed in four wings.

sentences.zh: 曲赦揚、南徐二州。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted for Yang and Southern Xu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was granted for Yang and Southern Xu provinces.

sentences.zh: 丁未，皇子生，少府劉蒙之子也。

translations.literal: On dingwei, an imperial prince was born—the son of Director of the Imperial Household Liu Meng.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei an imperial prince was born—the son of Director of the Imperial Household Liu Meng.

sentences.zh: 大赦，贓汙淫盜，悉皆原蕩，賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: A general amnesty; corruption, debauchery, and theft were all fully pardoned; those who had become heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed; corruption, debauchery, and theft were all fully pardoned, and those who had become heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以護軍將軍建安王休仁為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On renzi, General of the Guard Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was made General of Fast Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Prince Xiuren of Jian'an, General of the Guard, was made General of Fast Cavalry with privilege equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬深並賜死。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Prince Jingyou of Nanping, Prince Jingxian of Luling, and Marquis Jingshen of Annan were all ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Prince Jingyou of Nanping, Prince Jingxian of Luling, and Marquis Jingshen of Annan were all ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 時帝凶悖日甚，誅殺相繼，內外百官，不保首領。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor grew daily more vicious and perverse; executions followed one upon another, and officials within and without could not keep their heads.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor grew daily more vicious and perverse; executions followed one upon another, and officials within and without could not keep their heads.

sentences.zh: 先是，訛言湘中出天子，帝將南巡荊、湘以厭之，期旦誅除四叔，然後發引。

translations.literal: Earlier, a rumor had spread that a Son of Heaven would arise in Xiang; the emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang to suppress it, intending first to execute his four uncles at dawn, then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a rumor had spread that a Son of Heaven would arise in Xiang; the emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang to suppress it, intending first to execute his four uncles at dawn and then set out.

sentences.zh: 是夜湘東王彧與左右阮佃夫、王道隆、李道兒密結帝左右壽寂之、薑產之等十一人，謀共廢帝。

translations.literal: That night Prince Yu of Xiangdong, together with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er, secretly joined with eleven men among the emperor's personal attendants including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chananzhi, and together plotted to depose the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That night Prince Yu of Xiangdong, together with his attendants Ruan Tianfu, Wang Daolong, and Li Dao'er, secretly joined with eleven of the emperor's personal attendants, including Shou Jizhi and Jiang Chananzhi, and together plotted to depose him.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝好游華林園竹林堂，使婦人裸身相逐，有一婦人不從命，斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor loved to roam the Bamboo Grove Hall in Hualin Park, ordering women to run after one another naked; one woman refused and he beheaded her.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor loved to roam the Bamboo Grove Hall in Hualin Park, ordering women to chase one another naked; one woman refused and he beheaded her.

sentences.zh: 經少時，夜夢遊後堂，有一女子罵曰：「帝悖虐不道，明年不及熟矣。

translations.literal: Not long after, at night he dreamed he wandered the rear hall; a woman cursed him: "The emperor is perverse and cruel beyond measure; next year the grain will not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he dreamed at night that he wandered the rear hall; a woman cursed him: "The emperor is perverse and cruel beyond measure; next year the grain will not ripen.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，于宮中求得似所夢者一人戮之。

translations.literal: " Enraged, he searched the palace for someone resembling the woman in his dream and executed her.
translations.idiomatic: " Enraged, he searched the palace for someone resembling the woman in his dream and executed her.

sentences.zh: 其夕復夢所戮女罵曰：「汝枉殺我，已訴上帝。

translations.literal: That same night he dreamed again of the executed woman, who cursed: "You killed me wrongly; I have already appealed to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: That same night he dreamed again of the executed woman, who cursed: "You killed me wrongly; I have already appealed to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 」至是，巫覡云：「此堂有鬼」。

translations.literal: " By this time the shamans said: "This hall has a ghost."
translations.idiomatic: " By this time the shamans said: "This hall has a ghost."

sentences.zh: 帝與山陰公主及六宮彩女數百人隨群巫捕鬼，屏除侍衛，帝親自射之。

translations.literal: The emperor, together with the Princess of Shanyin and several hundred palace women, followed the shamans to hunt the ghost; the guards were dismissed, and the emperor shot at it himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, together with the Princess of Shanyin and several hundred palace women, followed the shamans to hunt the ghost; the guards were dismissed, and the emperor shot at it himself.

sentences.zh: 事畢，將奏靡靡之聲，壽寂之懷刀直入，薑產之為副，諸姬迸逸，廢帝亦走。

translations.literal: When the affair was done and seductive music was about to be played, Shou Jizhi, sword hidden in his robes, entered directly; Jiang Chananzhi followed as his second; the concubines fled in all directions, and the deposed emperor ran as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was done and seductive music was about to be played, Shou Jizhi, sword hidden in his robes, entered directly with Jiang Chananzhi as his second; the concubines fled in all directions, and the emperor ran as well.

sentences.zh: 追及之，大呼：「寂！

translations.literal: Pursuing him, he cried out: "Jizhi!
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing him, he cried out: "Jizhi!

sentences.zh: 寂！

translations.literal: "Jizhi!
translations.idiomatic: "Jizhi!

sentences.zh: 」如此者三，手不能舉，乃崩于華光殿，時年十七。

translations.literal: " Three times he called thus, but his hand could not rise; and he died in Huaguang Hall at the age of seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: " Three times he called thus, but his hand could not rise, and he died in Huaguang Hall at the age of seventeen.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后令奉湘東王彧纂承皇統。

translations.literal: The Empress Grand Dowager ordered that Prince Yu of Xiangdong succeed to the imperial succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Grand Dowager ordered that Prince Yu of Xiangdong succeed to the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 於是葬帝於丹陽秣陵縣南郊壇西。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling County, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor was buried west of the southern suburban altar in Moling County, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝蜂目鳥喙，長頸銳下，幼而狷急，在東宮每為孝武所責。

translations.literal: The emperor had eyes like a wasp's and a beak like a bird's, a long neck and sharp chin; from youth he was rash and impatient, and in the Eastern Palace was often rebuked by Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had eyes like a wasp's and a beak like a bird's, a long neck and sharp chin; from youth he was rash and impatient, and in the Eastern Palace was often rebuked by Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 孝武西巡，帝啟參承起居，書跡不謹，上詰讓之曰：「書不長進，此是一條耳。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's western tour, the emperor submitted memorials on daily affairs; his handwriting was careless, and the sovereign rebuked him: "Your calligraphy does not improve—this is one failing.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowu's western tour, the prince submitted memorials on daily affairs; his handwriting was careless, and the sovereign rebuked him: "Your calligraphy does not improve—this is one failing.

sentences.zh: 聞汝比素業都懈，狷戾日甚，何以頑固乃爾！

translations.literal: I hear that lately you have neglected your studies entirely and your perversity grows worse daily—how can you be so stubborn!
translations.idiomatic: I hear that lately you have neglected your studies entirely and your perversity grows worse daily—how can you be so stubborn!

sentences.zh: 」初踐阼，受璽紱，傲然無哀容。

translations.literal: " When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and cord, he was proud and showed no grief.
translations.idiomatic: " When he first ascended the throne and received the seal and cord, he was proud and showed no grief.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗退而歎曰：「昔魯昭不戚，叔孫請死，國家之禍，其在此乎。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong withdrew and sighed: "In old times Duke Zhao of Lu showed no sorrow, and Shusun asked to die—the ruin of the state, could it be here?
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong withdrew and sighed: "In old times Duke Zhao of Lu showed no sorrow, and Shusun asked to die—the ruin of the state, could it be here?

sentences.zh: 」帝始猶難諸大臣及戴法興等，既殺法興，諸大臣莫不震懾。

translations.literal: " At first the emperor still deferred to the great ministers and to Dai Fayxing and others; once Fayxing was killed, none of the great ministers failed to tremble in fear.
translations.idiomatic: " At first the emperor still deferred to the great ministers and to Dai Fayxing and others; once Fayxing was killed, none of the great ministers failed to tremble in fear.

sentences.zh: 於是又誅群公，元、凱以下，皆被毆捶牽曳，內外危懼，殿省騷然。

translations.literal: Then he executed the princes and dukes; from Yuan and Kai downward, all were beaten, dragged, and pulled about; within and without all were in peril, and the halls and ministries were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Then he executed the princes and dukes; from Yuan and Kai downward, all were beaten, dragged, and pulled about; within and without all were in peril, and the halls and ministries were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 太后疾篤，遣呼帝，帝曰：「病人間多鬼，可畏，那可往！

translations.literal: The empress dowager was gravely ill and sent for the emperor; the emperor said: "The rooms of the sick are full of ghosts—terrifying; how could I go!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was gravely ill and sent for the emperor; the emperor said: "The rooms of the sick are full of ghosts—terrifying; how could I go!

sentences.zh: 」太后怒，語侍者曰：「將刀來破我腹，那得生甯馨兒！

translations.literal: " The empress dowager in anger told her attendants: "Bring a knife to cut open my belly—how did I ever bear this Ningxin brat!
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager in anger told her attendants: "Bring a knife to cut open my belly—how did I ever bear this Ningxin brat!

sentences.zh: 」及太后崩後數日，帝夢太后謂曰：「汝不仁不孝，本無人君之相，子尚愚悖如此，亦非運祚所及。

translations.literal: " Several days after the empress dowager died, the emperor dreamed the empress dowager told him: "You are unkind and unfilial; you never had the aspect of a sovereign; Zishang is foolish and perverse as this—not the stuff of fortune's favor.
translations.idiomatic: " Several days after the empress dowager died, the emperor dreamed the empress dowager told him: "You are unkind and unfilial; you never had the aspect of a sovereign; Zishang is foolish and perverse as this—not the stuff of fortune's favor.

sentences.zh: 孝武險虐滅道，怨結人神，兒子雖多，並無天命；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu was vicious and cruel, extinguishing the Way, and resentment bound together men and gods; though he had many sons, none had Heaven's mandate;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu was vicious and cruel, extinguishing the Way, and resentment bound together men and gods; though he had many sons, none had Heaven's mandate;

sentences.zh: 大命所歸，應還文帝之子。

translations.literal: the great appointment should return to the sons of Emperor Wen."
translations.idiomatic: the great appointment should return to the sons of Emperor Wen."

sentences.zh: 」故帝聚諸叔都下，慮在外為患。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing trouble if they remained outside.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor gathered his uncles in the capital, fearing trouble if they remained outside.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主淫恣過度，謂帝曰：「妾與陛下雖男女有殊，俱托體先帝，陛下後宮數百，妾惟駙馬一人，事不均平，一何至此！

translations.literal: The Princess of Shanyin indulged licentiousness to excess; she told the emperor: "Your servant and Your Majesty differ in sex, yet both owe our bodies to the late emperor; Your Majesty's inner palace numbers in the hundreds, while I have but one consort—how uneven, how far it has come!
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shanyin indulged licentiousness to excess; she told the emperor: "Your servant and Your Majesty differ in sex, yet both owe our bodies to the late emperor; Your Majesty's inner palace numbers in the hundreds, while I have but one consort—how uneven, how far it has come!

sentences.zh: 」帝乃為立面首左右三十人，進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，湯沐邑二千戶，給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人。

translations.literal: " The emperor therefore set up thirty male favorites at her side, promoted her to Princess Long of Kuaiji Commandery with rank equal to a commandery prince, granted a fief of two thousand households, provided a full band of ceremonial music, and added twenty ceremonial guards with drawn swords.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor therefore set up thirty male favorites at her side, promoted her to Princess Long of Kuaiji Commandery with rank equal to a commandery prince, granted a fief of two thousand households, provided a full band of ceremonial music, and added twenty ceremonial guards with drawn swords.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，公主與朝臣常共陪輦。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, the princess and court ministers often shared the imperial carriage in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, the princess and court ministers often shared the imperial carriage in attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝少好讀書，頗識古事，粗有文才，自造孝武帝誄及雜篇章，往往有辭采。

translations.literal: From youth the emperor loved reading, knew ancient affairs fairly well, and had some literary talent; the dirge he composed for Emperor Xiaowu and various other pieces often showed real elegance.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the emperor loved reading, knew ancient affairs fairly well, and had some literary talent; the dirge he composed for Emperor Xiaowu and various other pieces often showed real elegance.

sentences.zh: 以魏武有發丘中郎將、摸金校尉，乃置此二官，以建安王休仁、山陽王休佑領之，其餘事蹟，分見諸列傳。

translations.literal: Because Cao Cao had had the Director of Tomb-Opening and the Commandant of Gold-Seeking, he established these two offices, which Prince Xiuren of Jian'an and Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang held; his other deeds are treated separately in the various biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cao Cao had had the Director of Tomb-Opening and the Commandant of Gold-Seeking, he established these two offices, which Prince Xiuren of Jian'an and Prince Xiuyou of Shanyang held; his other deeds are treated separately in the various biographies.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文帝幼年特秀，自稟君德。

translations.literal: Commentary: In youth Emperor Wen was uniquely gifted and from the first possessed the virtue of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In youth Emperor Wen was uniquely gifted and from the first possessed the virtue of a ruler.

sentences.zh: 及正位南面，歷年長久，綱維備舉，條禁明密，罰有恆科，爵無濫品。

translations.literal: Once he took the throne facing south, his reign lasted many years; the network of governance was fully maintained, regulations clear and strict, punishments had fixed standards, and ranks were not granted wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took the throne facing south, his reign lasted many years; the network of governance was fully maintained, regulations clear and strict, punishments had fixed standards, and ranks were not granted wantonly.

sentences.zh: 故能內清外晏，四海謐如。

translations.literal: Thus within was purity and without was peace; the four seas were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Thus within was purity and without was peace; the four seas were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 而授將遣師，事乖分閫。

translations.literal: Yet in appointing generals and dispatching armies, he failed to delegate command properly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in appointing generals and dispatching armies, he failed to delegate command properly.

sentences.zh: 才謝光武，而遙制兵略，至於攻戰日時，咸聽成旨，雖覆師喪旅，將非韓、白，而延寇蹙境，抑此之由。

translations.literal: His talent fell short of Emperor Guangwu's, yet he remotely controlled military strategy; even the day and hour of attacks were all as he decreed. Though armies were destroyed and troops lost—the generals were no Han Xin or Bai Qi—yet the enemy lingered and the borders were pressed inward; largely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: His talent fell short of Emperor Guangwu's, yet he remotely controlled military strategy; even the day and hour of attacks were all as he decreed. Though armies were destroyed and troops lost—the generals were no Han Xin or Bai Qi—yet the enemy lingered and the borders were pressed inward, largely for this reason.

sentences.zh: 及至言泄衾衽，難結凶豎，雖禍生非慮，蓋亦有以而然。

translations.literal: When words leaked from the bedchamber and enmity formed with a vicious youth, though disaster arose unforeseen, there were grounds for it.
translations.idiomatic: When words leaked from the bedchamber and enmity formed with a vicious youth, though disaster arose unforeseen, there were grounds for it.

sentences.zh: 夫盡人命以自養，蓋惟桀、紂之行；

translations.literal: To exhaust human lives for one's own pleasure is conduct fit only for Jie and Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust human lives for one's own pleasure is conduct fit only for Jie and Zhou;

sentences.zh: 觀夫大明之世，其將盡人命乎。

translations.literal: looking at the Daming era, was it not close to exhausting human lives?
translations.idiomatic: looking at the Daming era, was it not close to exhausting human lives?

sentences.zh: 雖周公之才之美，亦當終之以亂，由此言之，得歿亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: Even one with the beauty of the Duke of Zhou's talent would in the end have fallen to disorder; from this perspective, to die when he did was also a kind of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Even one with the beauty of the Duke of Zhou's talent would in the end have fallen to disorder; from this perspective, to die when he did was also a kind of fortune.

sentences.zh: 至如廢帝之事，行著於篇，假以中才之君，有一於此，足以致霣，況乎兼斯眾惡，不亡其可得乎！

translations.literal: As for the affairs of the Deposed Emperor, his deeds are plain in these pages; were an emperor of merely middling talent guilty of even one such thing, it would be enough to bring ruin—how much less when he combined all these evils; could he not have perished?
translations.idiomatic: As for the affairs of the Deposed Emperor, his deeds are plain in these pages; were an emperor of merely middling talent guilty of even one such thing, it would be enough to bring ruin—how much less when he combined all these evils; could he not have perished?
